diagnosis.root_cause: EPON0/7 is congested during peak usage: the port is carrying 912 Mbps currently, with a 948 Mbps peak against approximately 1 Gbps shared capacity. The customer's evening slowdown is therefore a shared PON contention problem rather than an optical, ONU, authentication, router, or OLT fault.
evidence: The complaint is time-dependent: service is acceptable during the day and degrades in the evening, which is characteristic of peak-period contention.
The customer's ONU is online and responding, with RX power -21.27 dBm and TX power 2.37 dBm, both within the calibrated healthy ranges.
Seven days of optical telemetry are stable: RX remains approximately -21 dBm, TX remains near 2.3 dBm, distance is constant at 167 m, and TX bias current remains within the healthy 9.5-13.0 mA range.
The customer has only 2 sessions in 24 hours and 16 in 7 days, with average duration about 11.9 hours, so there is no session flapping or authentication instability.
RADIUS data is present and consistent with CRM, VLAN 1017 is correctly provisioned, and the ONU exchange completes successfully.
The OLT and router are reachable and healthy; OLT CPU, memory, temperature, and router heartbeat do not indicate an infrastructure failure.
All probed ONUs on EPON0/7 are online, so this is not a PON-wide outage or port failure.

EPON0/7 has 47 subscribers and is operating near line rate, with 912 Mbps current traffic, 948 Mbps peak traffic, and 488 Mbps average traffic, providing direct evidence of peak shared-port congestion.

remediation.action: Confirm utilization and per-ONU traffic during the evening peak, identify heavy users, and apply appropriate bandwidth/QoS controls. Perform capacity relief by moving subscribers to a less-loaded PON port or splitting EPON0/7, and upgrade the access/uplink capacity if available. Do not replace the customer's ONU or fibre based on the current evidence; continue monitoring port utilization after remediation.

ground_truth.root_cause: EPON0/7 carries 47 customers and its evening load is reaching 912 Mbps against a 488 Mbps average, close to the port's shared capacity ceiling. Throughput degrades for everyone on the port during peak hours. No optical or authentication fault exists.
expected_reasoning: The complaint is time-of-day specific, which points at load rather than at a physical fault
RX is flat at -21.2 dBm inside the noise floor, and TX, bias, voltage and distance are all stable
The live probe shows every ONU on the port online with normal optical readings
RADIUS is clean and sessions are long and stable, so authentication is not involved
PON port traffic is at 912 Mbps against a 488 Mbps average
Daily traffic for this customer is roughly three times the network mean and rising, not falling
Every fault-driven degradation reduces traffic; congestion raises it, so the direction is the discriminator
The customer's own throughput series drops sharply during the same evening hours each day
The port carries 47 customers, at the top of the observed occupancy distribution
This is capacity exhaustion on a shared port, not a fault on any one line

expected_escalation.review_reason: EPON0/7 needs a capacity review; 47 customers on one port with evening load near ceiling

distractors: Multi-customer slowness resembles a splitter or feeder degradation
Elevated OLT CPU and temperature could be read as device stress causing the slowness
Reduced throughput in the speed series looks like a link problem
